text: **KRouter**（DSH CLI 插件）：把本机 Obsidian vault 中的 Markdown 知识接入 DeepSeek Harness。它注册七个只读工具，查询状态、偏好、更正、记忆、项目和全库内容，也提供别名建议。路由先检查人工维护的规范别名，再执行分层召回；结果附来源页与收据，找不到可信答案时明确返回未命中。适合希望多个编程 agent 共用本地项目记录、偏好和更正的用户。检索需要 Python 3 和 vault 路径；Obsidian 应用及 API key 均非检索必需。

**KRouter** (DSH CLI) connects a local Markdown vault to DeepSeek Harness. Seven read-only tools retrieve preferences, corrections, projects and memory, with cited sources and alias suggestions. Missing confident matches return no answer. Needs Python 3 and a vault path; no API key or Obsidian app.
想让 DeepSeek Harness 查本地项目笔记，并附上具体来源页。
DSH 能不能找回之前做过的决定和后来改过的结论？
我想让几个编程 agent 共用同一份 Markdown 知识库。
帮我按偏好、纠错记录或项目经历查以前的资料。
没有可靠记录时，让 agent 明确说知识库里没有。
希望 DSH 先按别名定位规范页面，避免命中旧说法。
How can my DSH agent retrieve local notes with cited sources?
I want coding agents to share local memory and correction history.
**KRouter** 的功能「DSH 路由工具」：注册七个只读工具，查询状态、偏好、更正、记忆、项目和全库内容，也可请求别名建议。状态工具无需 query，其余接收短 query。
**KRouter** 的功能「规范别名定位」：查询先匹配人工维护的规范别名表；命中时返回 canonical_source、canonical_id 和 how 等收据字段。
**KRouter** 的功能「分层本地召回」：偏好、更正、记忆、项目和全库路由按范围召回；专属范围没有可信命中时可扩展到全 vault，并标注范围变化。
**KRouter** 的功能「无结果字面搜索」：召回无足够置信结果时明确输出未命中，再退回 Markdown 字面搜索；输出限制行数并执行脱敏。
**KRouter** 的功能「别名建议」：未匹配规范来源时，suggest 路由返回候选别名作为搜索提示；候选不会被当成已确认的命中。
**KRouter** 的功能「Vault 状态查询」：状态工具返回首页状态、每日封存、自动化和备份信息，并将需主机处理的事项放入 host_action。
KRouter 的 DSH socket 只注册只读查询工具；添加该插件不会启动 nightly writer 定时任务。

dsh-krouter README · KRouter：**Your coding agents remember what you decided — and what you changed your mind about.**

Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and DeepSeek Harness share one memory: a folder of plain Markdown in [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md) that you can read and edit. Ask "how did we decide to ship?" and the agent answers with the page it came from. A correction replaces the old answer instead of competing with it. When the vault does not know, the agent is told so, rather than handed something close.

dsh-krouter README · KRouter：**Measured, not claimed.** On 200 held-out questions in English and Chinese that it was never tuned on, at default
settings, KRouter cites a wrong page 26% of the time; claude-mem 64%, basic-memory 78%. Of 80 questions the vault
cannot answer, KRouter refuses 47; the other two refuse none. Of 60 questions about a decision that was later
changed, it gets 50 right; they get 34 and 16. Neither of them can refuse or knows a page was replaced, so part of
that gap is by construction: plain full-text search given KRouter's two rules is level with it. What KRouter adds is
having those rules on by default, plus receipts and a vault you can edit. [How it was measured](docs/BENCHMARK.md#third-bench-200-held-out-questions-on-a-vault-nobody-tunes-on-2026-10-13) · [rerun it in one second](#check-it-yourself)

dsh-krouter README · Install：Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/398894496-arch/KRouter/main/scripts/bootstrap.ps1 | iex` · Claude Code plugin: `/plugin install krouter --marketplace 398894496-arch/KRouter` (Claude Code 2.1.275 or later; from a shell, `claude plugin install krouter --marketplace 398894496-arch/KRouter` needs 2.1.292). Third-party marketplaces do not auto-update: run `claude plugin update krouter@krouter`, or turn it on in `/plugin` → Marketplaces → krouter → Enable auto-update.

dsh-krouter README · Install：Rather look first? Nothing below changes your machine until the last line:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/398894496-arch/KRouter.git && cd KRouter
./scripts/first_run.sh                      # a receipt on the bundled sample vault
python3 scripts/bootstrap.py --dry-run      # every change the install would make, made nowhere
python3 scripts/bootstrap.py --vault ~/notes --no-timer   # install against your vault, nightly job off

dsh-krouter README · Install：Python 3 is the only requirement. The installer makes a vault (or uses yours with `--vault`, overwriting nothing), connects Claude Code and Codex to it through MCP, and stops there: lookup only, no questions, nothing leaves the machine. When you want it to start remembering, run the line it prints last (`bootstrap.py --ask`), which asks two questions.

dsh-krouter README · Five minutes later：1. Ask your agent: *"what did we decide about X last week?"* It answers from the vault, names the page, and says plainly when the vault has nothing on it.
2. **"Import the agent sessions already on this machine?"** (with `--ask`) On a yes, the last 7 days of Claude Code, Codex and Cursor agent sessions become pages, one per session: your questions and each turn's closing answer. Key-shaped text is redacted first, and nothing leaves the machine.
3. **"Have your model pull out what was decided?"** On a yes, the model you already use (a logged-in CLI or an API key) writes "what was decided, what changed" at the top of each recent session's page. The installer tells you how many characters that sends before it sends anything.
dsh-krouter README · Five minutes later：From then on a nightly job, which also asks first, imports yesterday, distills it, and keeps the vault tidy. Nothing needs maintaining.

dsh-krouter README · Is it for you?：**Yes**, if you use Claude Code, Codex, Cursor or DeepSeek Harness (often more than one), keep notes in Markdown or
would, and keep re-explaining the same decision to your agents. **No**, if you want semantic search over
embeddings, the last chat replayed into the next one, a hosted memory API, or a brain that is full on install.

**Not only for code:** the same story for short-video work, recorded the same way (Claude Code with the plugin, a

dsh-krouter README · Is it for you?：**Not needed:** Obsidian (it is an optional viewer), an alias table to maintain, an environment variable to set.
Already have a vault? `--vault` changes none of its files. The default is lookup only: no nightly job, no session
import.

dsh-krouter README · How it is different：| | KRouter | Typical agent memory |
|---|---|---|
| Where memory lives | Markdown pages you can open, edit, diff and sync | A database or vector store |
| After a correction | The new page replaces the old one, which is marked superseded | Old and new chunks both match; you hope the right one wins |
| When nothing matches | `recall: none` — the agent says the vault does not know | The nearest chunk, presented with confidence |
| Every answer | Carries its source page and a receipt | Usually unsourced |
| Who shares it | One vault for every agent on the machine (MCP, skill, rules) | Usually one tool |

dsh-krouter README · How it is different：**Coming from [claude-mem](https://github.com/thedotmack/claude-mem)?** Keep it. The importer has been run end to end against a live claude-mem 13.35.0 install. The installer finds its memory and offers to import it: session summaries become pages, and each project's decisions become one page you confirm. Your model can then sort those decisions into the ones still in force and the ones a later decision replaced, which claude-mem itself does not do. The Claude Code plugin also does what makes claude-mem feel like memory, in plain Markdown: when a session ends it is recorded, and when a new one starts, this repository's confirmed decisions and recent corrections come with it, each naming its page. Repositories are told apart by their path, never by folder name. Both happen only after you said yes to importing.

dsh-krouter README · What leaves your machine：Queries never do: lookup is a local SQLite full-text index, about 110 ms. Session import is local. Text goes to a model only for the steps you said yes to: distilling sessions and nightly upkeep. It goes to the CLI or API key you already use, and `--dry-run` shows the size first. Keys and pages marked secret are never sent or quoted. For the nightly writer, the API-key lane runs nothing on
your machine; CLI lanes differ in what they can read, and the install says which one you are choosing. Details:
[`SECURITY.md`](SECURITY.md).

dsh-krouter README · What leaves your machine：**Backups.** `backup.py init --dir <a folder that syncs elsewhere>` turns on a nightly encrypted archive of the whole
vault, history included, opened again each night before it counts. Point it at iCloud Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, a
Netdisk sync folder or a USB disk (or two of them); KRouter talks to no cloud. Why this and not syncing or pushing the
vault: [`DETAILS.md` → Backing up your vault](docs/DETAILS.md#backing-up-your-vault).

dsh-krouter README · Honest numbers：| Measured | Result |
|---|---|
| Refuses instead of guessing (public benches, CI) | Off-topic questions refused 12/12 (English) and 6/6 (Chinese) |
| Wrong citations on a vault nobody tuned on ([third bench](docs/BENCHMARK.md#third-bench-200-held-out-questions-on-a-vault-nobody-tunes-on-2026-10-13), 200 held-out questions, English and Chinese, with daily-log distractors; 95% intervals) | At its default: KRouter 26% [19, 33] wrong, 47 / 80 neighbour questions refused, 102 / 120 answerable right; plain full-text search 58% [52, 65]. **Against a careful baseline it is level, not ahead:** plain search with the same two rules (leave replaced pages out, refuse below a floor) at the same coverage cites 42 wrong pages to KRouter's 36 and gets 96 right to 102, but neither difference is significant (paired intervals: wrong rate [-10.2, +1.3] points, right [-2, +14]). On the same 200 questions at their defaults, claude-mem 13.39 cites a wrong page 64% of the time [58, 71] and basic-memory 0.23 78% [72, 84]; neither refuses any of the 80 neighbour questions; of 60 questions about a changed decision they get 34 and 16 right, KRouter 50 |

dsh-krouter README · Check it yourself：No install, no model, Python 3 only; the questions are in the repository and the numbers above come out in about a
second:

```bash
python3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout3 --ci                        # KRouter, with 95% intervals
python3 bench/memory_honesty/run.py --set heldout3 --vs-matched bm25-floor    # against BM25 + the same two rules
```
